citation.title: Differences in physiological response to an oral glucose tolerance test in adult Maasai men and women

population.description: 58 adult rural Maasai (29 men, 29 women) in Monduli district, Tanzania, without known or study-detected diabetes (pregnant women excluded); not screened as normal glucose tolerance (one man had impaired fasting glucose and three participants had impaired glucose tolerance), so unselected. Age and BMI are the printed means, SDs and observed ranges of all 58.

protocols.name: fasting_men
protocols.description: Fasting plasma glucose of the 29 Maasai men, drawn at the start of the OGTT day after an overnight fast (the 0 min sample); the paper gives no clock time and no number of hours fasted, so a 10 h fast, 08:00 and a 30-minute fasted run-in stand for the single sample. Mean age and BMI are Table 1's for this sex.

protocols.name: fasting_women
protocols.description: Fasting plasma glucose of the 29 Maasai women, drawn at the start of the OGTT day after an overnight fast (the 0 min sample); the paper gives no clock time and no number of hours fasted, so a 10 h fast, 08:00 and a 30-minute fasted run-in stand for the single sample. Mean age and BMI are Table 1's for this sex.

protocols.name: ogtt_men
protocols.description: OGTT of the 29 Maasai men: the 0 min sample was drawn after an overnight fast and the 75 g glucose in 300 mL water was taken within 5 min after it (Methods); samples at 0, 10, 30, 60, 90 and 120 min after it. The paper gives no clock time and no hours fasted, so a 30-minute fasted run-in, 10 h fast and 08:00 are assumed: the glucose is at arm minute 30, so paper minute T is arm minute 30 + T (samples at arm minutes 30, 40, 60, 90, 120, 150; arm 151 min). Participants sat; they could walk slowly to a restroom on request. Mean age and BMI are Table 1's for this sex.

protocols.name: ogtt_women
protocols.description: OGTT of the 29 Maasai women: the 0 min sample was drawn after an overnight fast and the 75 g glucose in 300 mL water was taken within 5 min after it (Methods); samples at 0, 10, 30, 60, 90 and 120 min after it. The paper gives no clock time and no hours fasted, so a 30-minute fasted run-in, 10 h fast and 08:00 are assumed: the glucose is at arm minute 30, so paper minute T is arm minute 30 + T (samples at arm minutes 30, 40, 60, 90, 120, 150; arm 151 min). Participants sat; they could walk slowly to a restroom on request. Mean age and BMI are Table 1's for this sex.

fasting GLP-1 by sex (Table 2), geometric mean with 95% CI, a lone fasting level of total GLP-1 with no change from it printed

insulin total AUC by sex (Table 2, Figure 1), geometric mean with 95% CI: printed 'nmol/L x min' (37,739 and 39,968) beside insulin in pmol/L (fasting 51, 2 h 179); over 120 min the printed unit gives a mean insulin of about 314 nmol/L, which fails the range check, so the unit is a misprint the paper does not correct

early phase insulin, C-peptide, GIP and GLP-1 secretion (iAUC of first 30 min, baseline-subtracted per person), geometric means with 95% CI (Table 2); an incremental area can be negative per person and is not a geometric area of the marker
HOMA-IR, disposition index, Matsuda index, insulin/glucagon ratio (Table 2)
